doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
title: Fifty-second Street and New York's music scene
summary: He lists the clubs and acts on 52nd Street and Birdland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, he was fortunate. But that’s when places like Birdland opened up. Of course, Kelly’s Stable on 52nd Street, they had live music in there. They had Nat King Cole trio, Coleman Hawkins, Teddy Wilson, they had everybody. And Ben Webster, Don Byas, they were

all playing in there at one time. Then you’d go down the street to the Hickory House, there would be Billy Taylor and his trio, Buddy Rich would be playing with Joe Marsala, I think that was the band he played with. End of CD #3 Then you go to the Famous Door, there would be the Count Basie band. Across the street there would be Ryan’s, Jimmy Ryan’s. There would be Wilbur de Paris, brothers, they would have a band over there. Next door would be the Three Deuces, John Kirby. Oh, it was so much music in New York in those days.
